questions.question: I look forward to ______ you soon.
questions.explanation: Phrasal verb 'look forward to' is followed by a gerund (-ing form), not a bare infinitive.

questions.question: She avoided ______ to the stranger.
questions.explanation: The verb 'avoid' is followed by a gerund, not an infinitive.

questions.question: Would you mind ______ the door?
questions.explanation: 'Would you mind' is always followed by a gerund (-ing form).

questions.question: He made me ______ for two hours.
questions.explanation: The causative verb 'make' takes a bare infinitive (wait without 'to') in active voice.

questions.question: I saw him ______ the bicycle.
questions.explanation: Verbs of perception (see, hear, watch) take bare infinitive or participle ('steal').

questions.question: He prevented me from ______ the gate.
questions.explanation: Prepositions are followed by gerunds: 'from entering'.

questions.question: There is no harm in ______ the truth.
He gave up ______ after his illness.
questions.explanation: Phrasal verb 'give up' takes a gerund: 'give up smoking'.

questions.question: She is fond of ______ novels.
questions.explanation: Preposition 'of' takes a gerund: 'fond of reading'.

questions.question: It is no use ______ over spilt milk.
questions.explanation: The idiomatic phrase 'It is no use' takes a gerund ('crying').

questions.question: It is worth ______ this exhibition.
questions.explanation: 'Worth' is followed by a gerund ('worth visiting').

questions.question: He is keen on ______ French.
questions.explanation: Preposition 'on' takes a gerund: 'keen on learning'.

questions.question: She was accused of ______ money.
questions.explanation: Preposition 'of' takes a gerund: 'accused of stealing'.

questions.question: I am tired of ______ to his excuses.
questions.explanation: Preposition 'of' takes a gerund: 'tired of listening'.

questions.question: We are looking forward to ______ the exam results.
With a view to ______ his English, he joined a course.
questions.explanation: 'With a view to' is always followed by a gerund ('improving').

questions.question: He is used to ______ up late.
questions.explanation: 'Be used to' (accustomed to) takes a gerund ('staying').

questions.question: I remember ______ him at the conference last year.
questions.explanation: 'Remember + gerund' refers to recalling a past memory.

questions.question: Please remember ______ the front door before leaving.
questions.explanation: 'Remember + infinitive' means not to forget a future duty/obligation.

questions.question: He stopped ______ when the teacher entered the classroom.
questions.explanation: 'Stop + gerund' means to discontinue an action altogether.

questions.question: On his way home, he stopped ______ some fruits.
questions.explanation: 'Stop + infinitive' means halting in order to do something.

questions.question: I regret ______ you that your application was rejected.
questions.explanation: 'Regret to inform' is used when giving bad news formally.

questions.question: He regretted ______ so much money on gambling.
questions.explanation: 'Regret + gerund' means feeling sorry about a past action.

questions.question: He cannot help ______ at the funny clown.
questions.explanation: 'Cannot help' is followed by a gerund ('laughing').

questions.question: I cannot bear ______ him suffer like this.
Let him ______ whatever he wants.
questions.explanation: 'Let' is followed by a bare infinitive ('do').

questions.question: He did nothing but ______ all day.
questions.explanation: After 'did nothing but...', a bare infinitive is used ('sleep').

questions.question: I heard her ______ a sweet song.
questions.explanation: Verbs of perception like 'hear' take bare infinitive ('sing').

questions.question: He was made ______ the speech.
questions.explanation: In passive voice, 'make' takes full infinitive with 'to' ('was made to deliver').

questions.question: He was seen ______ the compound wall.
questions.explanation: In passive voice, 'see' takes full infinitive ('was seen to scale').

questions.question: She refused ______ the bribe.
questions.explanation: 'Refuse' is followed by a full infinitive with 'to' ('to accept').

questions.question: She decided ______ for the IAS exam.
He managed ______ the train just in time.
He has enough sense ______ the danger.
This mango is fit ______.
questions.explanation: Adjective 'fit' takes infinitive of purpose/state ('to eat').

questions.question: ______ is believing.
questions.explanation: Famous proverb: 'Seeing is believing' (subject and complement are gerunds).

questions.question: ______ is injurious to health.
questions.explanation: Gerund as subject of the sentence: 'Smoking is injurious to health.'

questions.question: ______ is human; to forgive, divine.
questions.explanation: Proverb: 'To err is human; to forgive, divine' (infinitive as subject).

questions.question: He is afraid of ______ in the dark.
questions.explanation: Preposition 'of' takes a gerund: 'afraid of walking'.

questions.question: She is good at ______ portraits.
questions.explanation: Preposition 'at' takes a gerund: 'good at drawing'.

questions.question: He insisted on ______ the bill.
questions.explanation: Preposition 'on' takes a gerund: 'insisted on paying'.

questions.question: They succeeded in ______ the summit.
questions.explanation: Preposition 'in' takes a gerund: 'succeeded in reaching'.

questions.question: She is capable of ______ the heavy load.
questions.explanation: Preposition 'of' takes a gerund: 'capable of carrying'.

questions.question: He desisted from ______ falsehoods.
questions.explanation: Preposition 'from' takes a gerund: 'desisted from speaking'.

questions.question: He is accustomed to ______ in hot weather.
I object to your ______ without asking.
questions.explanation: 'Object to' takes a possessive adjective + gerund ('your leaving').

questions.question: He risked ______ his life to save the drowning child.
Would you mind ______ me your pen?
He is dedicated to ______ the poor.
She is prone to ______ silly errors.
I look forward to ______ from you.
With an eye to ______ his business, he visited Dubai.
questions.explanation: 'With an eye to' takes a gerund ('expanding').

questions.question: He has a penchant for ______ stamps.
She has a passion for ______ classical dance.
She felt the floor ______ during the earthquake.
I notice him ______ the gate quietly.
You need not ______ there alone.
questions.explanation: Modal auxiliary 'need not' takes bare infinitive 'go'.

questions.question: He had better ______ the matter right now.
She would rather ______ tea than coffee.
She was helped ______ the luggage.
questions.explanation: Passive of 'help' takes full infinitive 'to carry'.

questions.question: He offered ______ us in our work.
I can't afford ______ such a costly phone.
He is good at ______ portraits.
questions.explanation: Preposition 'at' is followed by a gerund ('drawing').

questions.question: She prevented me from ______ the gate.
I look forward to ______ you soon.
She is looking forward to ______ her degree.
He is addicted to ______ video games.
He is accustomed to ______ hard in the sun.
With a view to ______ his business, he traveled abroad.
questions.explanation: 'With a view to' takes a gerund ('expanding').

questions.question: I object to your ______ during the lecture.
questions.explanation: 'Object to' takes a possessive + gerund ('your talking').

questions.question: It is no use ______ over lost opportunities.
questions.explanation: 'It is no use' takes a gerund ('crying').

questions.question: He gave up ______ after his illness.
questions.explanation: Phrasal verb 'give up' takes a gerund ('smoking').

questions.question: I cannot help ______ at his silly mistakes.
I remember ______ this place when I was a child.
questions.explanation: 'Remember + gerund' refers to a past memory ('visiting').

questions.question: Please remember ______ the front door before leaving.
questions.explanation: 'Remember + infinitive' refers to a future obligation ('to lock').

questions.question: He stopped ______ when the bell rang.
questions.explanation: 'Stop + gerund' means to discontinue an activity ('writing').

questions.question: On his way to office, he stopped ______ a newspaper.
questions.explanation: 'Stop + infinitive' means halting in order to do something ('to buy').

questions.question: I regret ______ you that the flight has been cancelled.
questions.explanation: 'Regret to inform' is used when giving formal bad news.

questions.question: He regretted ______ his valuable time on games.
questions.explanation: 'Regret + gerund' expresses sorrow for a past action ('wasting').

questions.question: The teacher made him ______ on the bench.
questions.explanation: Causative 'make' in active voice takes a bare infinitive ('stand').

questions.question: He was made ______ the entire poem.
questions.explanation: In passive voice, 'make' takes full infinitive with 'to' ('to recite').

questions.question: I saw the thief ______ the wall.
questions.explanation: Verbs of perception take bare infinitive ('scale').

questions.question: He was seen ______ the compound wall.
questions.explanation: Passive perception verb takes full infinitive ('to scale').

questions.question: We heard her ______ a sweet song.
She was heard ______ a sweet song.
He did nothing but ______ all afternoon.
questions.explanation: After 'did nothing but', use bare infinitive ('sleep').

questions.question: How dare you ______ my confidential files?
She decided ______ for the civil services examination.
He is too proud ______ his mistake.
______ is injurious to health.
questions.explanation: Gerund as subject: 'Smoking is injurious to health.'
